capabilities.summary: A host outside the engine's address space can call it: a version to check, memory to allocate, and memory to give back.
capabilities.note: The native host links the engine and calls it directly, so it never crosses this boundary. Not a gap; a different shape of host.

capabilities.summary: A compute graph or a single preset call can be executed on its own, without a model or a run, which is what backs the authoring API.
capabilities.note: Pinned by the shared vectors above, run natively and under WASM with TypeScript counterparts, rather than by host vectors that would restate them. The native CLI runs models; it exposes no value or compute API.

capabilities.summary: A model is parsed, validated, indexed, and lowered once, and many runs execute against that one prepared form.
capabilities.note: TypeScript exposes this as prepareModel/PreparedModel.release(), and "WASM model handle runs many runtimes against one prepared model" in abi.zig pins the engine side. The native host prepares a model and runs it once; no vector shows it reusing one, so its status is what the vectors earn and not what the code looks like it could do.

capabilities.summary: An action can take binding values from host code, and the runtime tells the hook what it owes and what it may read.
An action can hand its post-merge STATE to host code, and the outcome is recorded on the action rather than raised.
Actions run in the order the model's next rules select, across scenes when a route drives them, over one STATE.
A model can grow while it runs: an extend hook returns a model, it is merged before the action prepares, and every collision is an error rather than an override.
capabilities.note: Both hosts bound how many times a run may merge, because every merge retains the model it replaced: maxModelMerges on the WASM create request, --max-model-merges on the native CLI.
